text: Seven chapters assumed you already knew what to build. This one backs up a step: before you drag a single visual, know who's looking, and why.

Four questions, straight from Microsoft's own design guidance. How does your audience actually use this. What metrics change what they do next. What cultural or learned assumptions might shape how they read it. And what do they need to succeed — not what's merely interesting.
A dashboard sits on top of reports that already hold the detail. Readers can always drill deeper — so the dashboard itself should show only what someone needs to monitor, nothing more.
Write the answers down, even briefly — that becomes your reference point for every design choice the rest of this chapter covers. Next: choosing which KPIs actually earn a spot on the dashboard.
